quotes.text: Co-pilot doesn't create risk. It reveals it at scale. Think about how AI actually works in your tenant. It doesn't have its own secret set of keys. It doesn't bypass your security protocols. Instead, it precisely inherits the permissions of the person asking the question.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes Copilot risk as a mirror of existing permissions rather than a new threat.

quotes.text: The global admin was designed as a break glass role. It was supposed to be the emergency lever you pull when the building is on fire. Instead, it has become the default setting for convenience.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the core design failure behind over-assigned Global Admin roles.

quotes.text: You don't fix governance by adding policies. You fix it by removing power. If the architecture is the law, then the only way to change the law is to change who holds the keys.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable thesis that governance is about reducing standing privilege.

quotes.text: If an admin needs to change a global setting, they shouldn't have that power while they're checking their morning email. They should have to request it, justify it, and have it automatically expire after the task is done.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains just-in-time access in plain, practical terms.

quotes.text: Your executives define the strategy, but your global admins define the reality. It is time to align the two. Audit your shadow leadership layer today, because if you don't do it, co-pilot will eventually do it for you.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear call to action that sums up the episode.

takeaways: In Microsoft 365, real authority sits with whoever holds the Global Admin role, so over-assigned admin rights quietly override executive and security decisions.
Copilot does not create new risk; it inherits user permissions and surfaces years of oversharing and broken inheritance at scale.
A 30-day plan of inventorying privileged roles, cutting standing Global Admins by at least 80 percent and moving to just-in-time, scoped access realigns permissions with the org chart.
hook: Your org chart says the CEO is in charge, but your Microsoft 365 tenant says otherwise: dozens of Global Admins can override any policy with a single click. This episode is for IT leaders, security teams and executives who want to understand who really holds power in their tenant, and how to take it back with a 30-day plan before Copilot exposes the gaps.
